title: A common mistake: forgetting the quotes
idea: Text needs quotes. Without them, the computer thinks you mean something else and gets confused.

exercises.explanation: Text must be in quotes. print(Hello) is missing them — the computer won't know Hello is text.

exercises.prompt: To show a word, you can leave off the quotes.
exercises.explanation: Words are text, and text needs quotes. Without them you'll get an error.

exercises.prompt: Which one correctly shows the word Sun?
exercises.explanation: Only the first wraps the text in matching quotes inside the brackets.

exercises.prompt:
Fix this instruction so it correctly shows the word Moon:

print(____)
exercises.explanation: Add quotes around the text: print("Moon").

exercises.prompt: Why does print(apple) cause a problem, but print("apple") works?
options: Without quotes, the computer doesn't know apple is text
print only works with quotes on Tuesdays
exercises.explanation: Quotes are how you say 'this is text'. Without them, the computer looks for something called apple and fails.

exercises.prompt: Build a CORRECT instruction to show: river
exercises.explanation: Text in matching quotes, inside the brackets.

exercises.prompt: Which of these are missing their quotes? (pick all)
exercises.explanation: print(Dog) and print(Cat) have no quotes around the text — both would fail.

exercises.prompt: To show the word hi, it must be inside quotes.
exercises.explanation: Words are text, and text goes in quotes: print("hi").
Matching quotes, inside brackets. The others each break a rule you now know.

exercises.prompt: Write a full, correct instruction to show the word: start
exercises.explanation: print("start") — brackets and matching quotes, both present.
